utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have been informed that there are a few procedural matters. Let me just try to understand whether I was well informed about what they are. First, proposal in relation to the notification of witness order. The Chamber has received a copy of a letter that was sent to Mr. Zahar. Mr. Re, are you intending to respond to that letter or to make a counter-proposal, whatever?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will, of course, but I only received it -- I just want to say one thing, and no doubt it's an unintentional oversight by Mr. Emmerson, but one thing which he didn't refer to last week when he referred to the Milutinovic order was the counter-order by the Trial Chamber there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are going to introduce that in your response, then, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, that's the one requiring the Defence to notify the prediction of exhibits it intends to rely upon, and for the notification of the Defence, in case they haven't seen it - and I'm sure they haven't because they would have referred the Trial Chamber to it - it's a 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not seeking at this moment to discuss the matter. I just established that a proposal was made and whether we could receive a response from the Prosecution, and if the Prosecution would -- fears perhaps that the Defence was not fully informed, then I take it that the Prosecution will assist the Defence in getting full information so that the exchange of views on paper is as complete as possible and will guide the Chamber in deciding the matter, if there's no agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just in terms of what I can respond to. I can't respond today. I can respond on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Response on Wednesday. Then we would like to receive your response on Wednesday. Then I have understood that another issue would be whether the next two witnesses have already been proofed and whether there's any material available for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I simply clarify?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We know that they have already been proofed because certain proofing notes were provided last week before the orders were made about the taping of proofing sessions. The request was for clarification as to whether any proofing sessions were conducted after their arrival in The Hague and, therefore, whether there are further proofing notes to be forthcoming. We received, as I say, proofing notes, I think, on Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer is no. Mr. Di Fazio has emphatically told Mr. Emmerson before court that, and I don't know why he's raising it again. We've told him that there are none. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Mr. Di Fazio told me he didn't know. The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is no. That's at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, in which case once court rises, we can take a view on the material which has so far been served and make our position clear to the Prosecution as to provision of that material to the Trial Chamber. It's conceivable that as a result of that lack of clarity, Your Honours may receive the material slightly later than would otherwise be the case. But can I assure you this: It's short. It doesn't take very long to master.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then another issue I do understand the Chamber will consider that whether the order for audio-recording of proofing sessions, whether that would extend beyond the weekend. Of course, it's a temporary measure, that may be clear, but since we are still waiting for further submissions on the matter, the Chamber will consider during the next break whether or not to extend the order for audio-recording of proofing sessions. Then the fourth item I've got on my list is that there are Rule 68 matters to be raised, of which the Chamber would like to hear what exactly the issue is and also remind the party who would like to raise it that there may be a reason to go into private session. I'm not aware of anything, but ... Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Out of an abundance of caution, might we go into private session and then re-open it if I've been overcautious?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber was in private session for quite a while today since it had to discuss with the parties a lot of procedural issues which were characterised by the confidentiality of the information we were discussing. We will adjourn. We will resume at 4.00, Mr. Emmerson, unless you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do Your Honours still intend after this current break to give a decision in general on the interim arrangements for proofing sessions prior to the resolution of the issue to be argued in documents on Wednesday? In other words, not simply confined to the witness we've just been discussing in closed session but more generally. Because, for all we may know, there may be proofing sessions taking place as we speak that the Prosecution do not consider to be covered by the weekend order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the sake of transparency, I mean, we've taken the view you've made an interim ruling. There were two proofing sessions today, I've asked for them to be taped. There was one on the weekend with Witness 49 that has been taped. We take the view that until Your Honours have made a ruling contrary, which we hope that you do when you've received our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- written submissions, that we will tape them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's appreciated, I take it, also by the Defence. Then we'll adjourn until -- we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, are you ready to re-examine the witness? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I am, and I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming back after the weekend. I just want to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you put questions to the witness, I first wanted to apologise for our late start. You had to wait for quite a while, and, unfortunately, it's not the first time. Second, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I just want to ask you some questions about what you said when counsel for the Defence cross-examined you. Just two topics. Firstly, Mr. Guy-Smith asked you some questions concerning the KLA headquarters, and you said that there was one in the village -- in your village and that it had been a clinic, and during the war it served as a KLA headquarters. Do you remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poh.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is your answer ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were then asked some questions about travel authorisations. Now, did you ever go to this headquarters in your village or are you aware of any member of your family going to this headquarters to seek travel authorisations?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point, I'd object to that question as being compound, dealing with two separate subject matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you split it up? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever go to this KLA headquarters to seek travel authorisation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English booth is having a problem hearing the witness. We can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second. Witness, could you try to speak in the microphone? Perhaps you better repeat the question once, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Witness -- thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, I'll just repeat my question so that you -- you were just reminded again after that problem with the microphones. My question was this: Did you ever go to the headquarters, the headquarters in your village, to seek travel authorisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went with a member of my family, and we received authorisation. I went with my family member to take that authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In your questions on -- in your answers on Friday, you explained that your family members from time to time needed travel authorisations, you said, "Although personally I didn't go to get it." You then went on to say that you had gone to get travel authorisations with your brother and/or sister, but when that happened you stayed outside because you were scared and you were young. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, what I'd like to know is this: When you went with your brother and sister to get travel authorisations but were scared and remained outside, which village was this in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday I remembered it well, but now ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Do I understand that you can't recall the village where you went to get travel authorisations? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village where I was, in Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On Friday, you were asked questions by Mr. Guy-Smith about this issue and Mr. Guy-Smith put this question to you and you gave this answer, and I'll read it out to you so listen to what is being said: Question by Mr. Guy-Smith: "In the statement of 2004 you weren't scared, were you? And you used this, and by 'this,' I mean getting travel authorisation as a basis for identifying Idriz Balaj as Toger. Isn't that what you did?" And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And your answer was this: "What I said is that I saw him while the headquarters was there, but I didn't say that I went to that place personally to get a travel authorisation." So what you said on Friday was that you said to some investigator in a statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm going to object to Mr. Di Fazio testifying at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you formulate your question in such a way that you do not tell the witness what he said to the investigator. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Quite apart from what you said to anyone in a statement, did you see him, namely, Toger, in fact on any occasions that you went to get travel authorisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. You were asked some questions about -- MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps we should go into private session very briefly, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since I have no further questions for you and my colleagues also have no further questions for you, Witness, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague and to answer all the questions that are put to you, and I wish you a safe trip home again. You may now follow Madam Usher, who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kearney. Then protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same; that is, face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. Madam Usher left the courtroom so it's difficult to instruct her to bring the witness in. Yes. Then perhaps we could use our time -- Madam Registrar, are there any exhibits pending for admission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Witness 4, because we will not use your own name, but we will use a pseudonym. Witness 4, before you give evidence in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please be seated. I wanted to inform you that we are not only not using your name, but your face cannot be seen by the outside world, neither can your voice be heard by the outside world. Madam Registrar, usually it takes 20 minutes to adapt the voice distortion, but here it has been checked prior. Then, Witness 4, you'll first be examined by Mr. Kearney, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. At the outset, I'd like to move into private session for the purposes of identifying this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness number 4, in 1998 you've told us about how big your family was. I want to ask you simply if at that time your father was alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When was it he died, if you could tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: My father died in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the cause of his death, if you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Kearney, I'll ask for a redaction, and we'll go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in an abundance of caution, the next questions about his occupation, the Court may want to hear in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll move back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness 4, after your father's death, did Mr. Prascevic continue to have a relationship with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And could you please tell us about that relationship. What was the nature of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: After my father died we needed things. We needed tools to work the land and also foodstuff, things to buy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in an abundance of caution, the next area may be best handled in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- or, Witness 4, let me rephrase that last question or say it again. After this first visit by the men in your home, was there another visit after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long after the first visit was that second visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I think it was one week or two weeks later. I'm not sure. I didn't count the days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, this next visit, when did it happen? What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was about 10 p.m., at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, if you could, during this second visit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When they came for the second visit, we were at home, asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In your home, how did the members of your family sleep in relation to each other? Were there separate rooms for girls, boys? How did the sleeping arrangements work, please, in your home during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The brothers slept together, and my mother and the sisters slept in another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During this next visit that we're talking about, were you asleep when the men arrived or were you awake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, you were asleep? Or you were awake when they came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We were asleep, but when they came they woke us up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw or heard after you were awakened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They came inside, and there was still one of them who was keeping guard at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did the men want, if you know, during this visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: During this visit, well, I don't know because they went to my mother and my sisters. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What happened after the men went to your mother and your sisters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We heard this name being repeated over and over again, "Toger," "Toger."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was saying this name over and over again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was it one of your sisters or your mother, or was it one of the men who entered your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. It was a man who was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You indicated that there was another guard posted at your door during this visit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you get a look at this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please describe what he was wearing, for us, and if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He was wearing a mask and army clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Describe the army clothes for us, please. What colour were they? Did they have any insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Well, they were military clothes, and I can't remember whether they had any insignia on -- KLA insignia, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were they members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: That's what I think. And this is what I thought later, as a matter of fact, because at that moment I didn't know what to think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned that you heard the name Toger being used during this visit by the armed men. Or during the manner -- excuse me. In what manner was that name being used, please, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I don't know how they used the name, but I remember one of the soldiers that was there, one of his soldiers, called him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned that this man who guarded your door during this visit was wearing military-style clothing. Did he have any military-style arms, or weapons, with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please describe those for us, if you could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Well, at that time there was no electricity, so I couldn't see clearly what kind of gun they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he have some type of gun with him, this gentleman that was guarding you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He did have a gun, and it was a big one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did the men stay in your home on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly but probably half an hour, one hour. As I told you, I'm not sure how long they stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And do you know what the purpose of this visit was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: That night when they came, they told my mother that they wanted to take my sister with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And is this something you heard that night or is this something that your mother told you at some -- at a later point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. It was in the morning that my mother told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Your mother told you that they wanted to take your sister. Did she tell you why they wanted to take your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, because Toger had told her that each family has to have a soldier in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your mother indicate to you if any of the men who came into your home on this night identified themselves to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did she tell you in that regard, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When I spoke with my mother, she said that one person had told her, I am Togeri, and that he had asked for the daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Without using a proper name, please tell us which daughter it was that this man named Toger wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Toger was asking for S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your mum tell you anything about who was in charge of these men when they came into your home that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: You mean that night?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Did she tell you anything about who she thought to be in charge of these men?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, at this point I've refrained from objecting, but I'm interposing my usual objection because I figure that the Chamber would respond in the usual way. But we've had now an outstanding amount of hearsay, and I understand the Chamber will take it in due course and give it whatever weight is due. Now we're moving into an area where the level of speculation and lack of foundation is such that in the absence of some factual information prior to such a question being answered, I think that it's beyond being fatal from the standpoint of a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was whether the mother told anything to the mother. That's a permissible question. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness number 4, do you have my question in mind or shall I repeat it for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: If you could, please, repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your mother tell you anything about who she thought to be in charge of these men when they entered your home to take your sister S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: From what my mother told me the next day, she said, There is this person called Togeri, and he had told her that he wanted to take her daughter away as every family had to have someone in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your mother tell you how she herself felt about her daughter being taken by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: After we spoke with my mother, my mother told me, told us, that she didn't want to let her go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That night when the men came for sister S, did they, in fact, take your sister with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see sister S again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I'm not sure when she came back, but it was four days later that she visited us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you home on that occasion when she came back to visit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Four days later when your sister came back to visit you, were you at home at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What time of the day or night was it that your sister came back on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please tell us about that visit, if you could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When she came, so it was my sister S, with Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How do you know that -- when your sister came back to the home, was she with someone? Was she alone or with someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: She was with Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how is it you know that the person she was with was Toger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Because my mother had told us about what had happened that night and we started to learn about who this person was, I mean Togeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was it that you learned about this person Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: My sister came, as I said, she came inside while he left in his car. He was a little further away from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He was wearing black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The black clothes he was wearing, were they civilian in nature or were they military in nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. They were military.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How about your sister? What was she wearing when she came back to your home after she had been taken initially by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: My sister was also wearing special unit clothes, black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were they military in nature or were they civilian in nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Special unit clothes, black.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say "special unit clothes," what do you mean, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: At that time I learned this from my sister, that these are clothes that the special unit wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your sister tell you what the name of the special unit was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. We just asked her, What kind of clothes are these, because we had never seen them before, and then she told us what they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I'm looking at the clock. We need a break. Would this be a suitable moment or would you find another suitable moment within the next couple of minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This would be fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then at the same time, Mr. Kearney, I see the witness was scheduled for one hour and a half. You started your examination-in-chief, without major interruptions, at 23 minutes past 4.00. That means that you're close to five-quarters of an hour now. From what this Chamber could speculate on the basis of the statement, you might not be able to conclude in the next 18 minutes, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Yes, I do understand that, but I express again my concern, what seems to be a contagious disease. We stand adjourned until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness 4, when we left off, we were talking about your sister's visit back to your home. You were talking about the special unit clothes that she was wearing. I want to ask you if, at that time, you had seen in your village, or in your area, regular KLA soldiers anywhere on the roads or in the villages during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No, I had not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When your sister came back to see you after she had been taken, what was her demeanour or attitude, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: You mean my sister, what kind of demeanour she had when she came back?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The day she came back, she said that she had been brought there to take some clothes. It was just a short visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she seem happy, sad? Did she have any kind of a different demeanour than she had the last time you had seen her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I couldn't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: This special unit clothing she was wearing, did it have any insignia on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes. KLA insignia on the arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Would you recognise that insignia if you saw it again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the Court's permission, I'd like to show the witness Exhibit number P9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that similar to the patch she was wearing or the insignia she was wearing on the day in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Before that day when you saw it on your sister's clothing, had you ever seen that patch, or insignia, before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The first time when they came, the first time, I think I saw it, but as I told you, I was not paying too much attention to those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After that first time the men came to your home, which you've told us about, were there other visits by these men to your home before your sister S was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Before they took my sister? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many times these men came to your home during that period, from the first time they came until they took your sister S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I remember the first time they came when they said they had come to search the house for guns and take some money, and then the second time when they took my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On either of these visits to your home that you've described for us, did you recognise any of the men who came, besides Toger?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to object. That misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question, Your Honour, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Besides the gentleman that you've referred to as Toger, among the other people who came to your home on either of the occasions you've told us about, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I'm saying that we recognised only Toger at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your sister tell you anything else during this first visit to your home after she had been taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The first time they took her, she wasn't saying anything to us. Just where she was staying and what she was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And at some point that first -- during that first visit, did she leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Your sister. After the first visit was concluded, did she leave your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How did she leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, before we continue there, I'd like to seek some clarification of one of the previous answers. Witness 4, you said: "The first time they took her, she wasn't saying anything to us. Just where she was staying and what she was doing." Where did she say she was staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we asked her, she said that she was staying in Irzniq village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did she say she was doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She said, We are staying at the Irzniq school, the old school, as they call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question was what she said she was doing, apart from where she was staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time she came, she did not tell us lots of things. She just said that, We are staying there, and this and that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "And this and that," could you be a bit more explicit about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I mean is that when a person doesn't want to tell you things, says, This and that, and this is what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: She mentioned an old school that she was staying in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you know which building she was talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What building was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The old school in Irzniq. That's what they used to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know who, if anyone, was using that old school building during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: No, during the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We had heard also from our sister that the army was staying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Which army was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How did your sister -- how was it your sister left your home after this first visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: She said she did not have much time to stay; she had to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how, physically, did she leave? Did she go on foot? Did she go in a vehicle? How did she leave your home that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: By car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Whose car was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Toger's car. It was a Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see him take her away on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: That day he stayed there a little bit farther from the house. He did not go anywhere; he just waited a little bit farther away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say "a little farther away," how far away from your home was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: About 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he by himself or was he with someone in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I couldn't see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did he stay in that location before he drove your sister away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: If we're talking about the first visit, he did not stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you estimate how long he was there, for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: About 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you able to see him during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you able to see this man you're referring to as Toger during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When my sister got out of the house to go with him, she went there, because he was, as I said, 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you see him at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The Toger, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After that first visit, did you see your sister again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long after the first visit did you see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I'm not sure how long after it was, but maybe one week or two weeks after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During this second visit, how did your sister arrive to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Toger brought him [sic] in his car. He left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see that, Witness 4? Did you see this gentleman named Toger drop your sister off on this second visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During this second visit, did you get a chance to talk with your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Not at that moment, no. After she came inside the house -- into the house and she stayed for some time there, then I could speak to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was this second visit shorter or longer than the first visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The second visit was much longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did she tell you, if anything, about where she had been and what she was doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: After we asked her where she was staying and what she was doing, she told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was it that she told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: She said that there was a prison in Janic -- Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was this prison run by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And when you use the term "Irzniq," are you referring also to -- or is that village also named Rznic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your sister tell you anything about what she saw in this prison in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The mother said that she saw some prisoners of young and old age.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] S, my sister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she tell you how many prisoners she saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she tell you anything about what she had done or what her orders were, in general, as a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes. She talked to us. She said that she had received orders from Togeri to kill somebody, and then if she didn't kill him, then he would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she tell you who, if anyone, was the commander of the KLA in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After this second visit was concluded, how was it your sister left the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: After the last visit, it was about 3.00 in the afternoon, she told me that she should go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how was it she left? Did she leave on foot? Did she leave in a car? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: She went by foot. I saw her off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, that you saw her off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I accompanied her. I went together with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How far did you go with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We went up to a place called Vohu i Ratishit. That's how it is called.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: At some point, did you leave her that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After leaving her that day, did you ever see Toger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Tell us about that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The translation is missing. Witness, we do not receive your translation at this moment, I should say the translation of your words. You were asked whether after you left your sister that day, whether you ever saw Toger. You answered yes, and you were invited to tell us about it. Could you please repeat your answer? You started to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I came back, after I accompanied my sister, I came back home. After about 10, 15 minutes, then Toger came with the Niva car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with Toger during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please tell us what was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He said, Why was my sister late? I told him that she had just left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there any further conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. No, no, not anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you had this conversation with this person named Toger, how far from you was he? Were you -- please tell us, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I don't remember, but probably 7, 8, 9 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What time of the day was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was about 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you see his face at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness number 4, after sister S was taken, was another family member of yours taken from your home as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, at this point I'm going to object to the manner of the question that's been put to the witness, because we have a sister who has come and gone, and come and gone, a number of times. So it's, if anything, vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could specify a bit more which family member you had in mind, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: First, I remember the witness having said, instead of the second visit, her last visit, which makes me ask: Was the second visit her last visit, or did you see her again there or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I saw her only on these two occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just to follow up on that question, after this second visit by sister S you told us about, have you ever seen your sister again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After this last visit by sister S, did a group of men come back to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long after the last visit of sister S was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but probably after two, three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness number 4, can you tell us anything about what time of year this was, this visit we're about to talk about? So it's two to three weeks after the last visit of sister S. Can you tell us what month or what season of 1998 this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I remember it was autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And beyond that, can you be any more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I remember at that time we wanted to go away and we were harvesting the corn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Describe for us, please, what happened when this group of men came to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They came to us, and we were told to go and take permission if we wanted to go away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Describe these men, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Do you want me to mention their names?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, if you know them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: One was Togeri. Aslan Rexhepi, Sokol Zefi and Arush Islami.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What time of the day or night was this visit we're talking about now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon, probably 4.00. 4.00 or 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said at some point during this visit, someone told you that you needed permission to leave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was it that made that statement, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We wanted to go away and to go to make some visits, and we were told that we needed to take permission before we would leave the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say "we wanted to go away," who are you talking about, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: My family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where was it that you wanted to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We wanted to visit -- can we mention the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: May we go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's perhaps -- I don't know what the answer will be, so therefore -- perhaps we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness 4, what I'm asking you, simply, is where did you hear that? Where did you hear that you needed permission to make that trip you've just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We had -- this was only hearsay. Nobody had told us directly this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And after you heard this, that you needed to get permission to travel, did you attempt to get permission to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We went -- can I mention names or can I speak without mentioning names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can give names unless you are hesitant to do so because you feel that there may be a security risk involved for the persons whose name you're giving; and if that is the case, then you can address me and we could consider to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we went to take permission in the village, Aslan Rexhepi and Sokol Zefi were the people who should give us permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where in the village did you go to get this permission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: We went to the village, Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And, Witness 4, we understand that, but was there a certain place within the village of Ratis, a certain building or somewhere that you went, in particular, to go to seek this permission to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where within the village of Ratis did you go to try and get that permission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I went to a shop, to a shop. That's the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And who was in this shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Aslan Rexhepi, Sokol Zefi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What type of shop was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was a shop of housery [as interpreted], something like this. It's a normal shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And during the war, was it operating as a normal shop or was it operating as something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. It was used as a staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand your answer. Could you repeat your answer, please? It was used as what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was used as headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: For whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was used as a headquarters for the village to control what was happening in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And the headquarters for what organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The headquarters of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you went to this headquarters to get permission and you saw Aslan Rexhepi and Sokol Zefi, did you talk with them about getting permission to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They issued a document for me to go. They issued a document to go only as far as that village, not beyond that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you describe that document for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was a piece of paper, normal piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did it have any writings or pictures or graphs, or anything else, or any other image on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No, no. It was simply written by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was it signed by, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: It was signed by Aslan Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you met Aslan Rexhepi that day, was he in civilian clothes or was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He was wearing army clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, describe them for us, please? Which army, and what type of clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: He was wearing sort of army clothes, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were there any insignia on this camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: The KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: This camouflage uniform that you saw Mr. Rexhepi wearing on the day in question, was it different than the uniform that you'd seen your sister wearing and you'd seen Toger wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, it was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After you received this travel document, did you actually try and take this trip that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did this travel document work? Along the way, did you present that document to someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: When we were stopped by somebody, then we had to show the document, to tell them where we were going to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How many times did you have to show this document on the road to -- on the way to Bucan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Only once, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And who was it that asked for it or who was it that you showed this document to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: A soldier. I don't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: A soldier of which army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was -- where was it that you showed this KLA soldier your travel document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Can I mention the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the same as I said before. If you have any concerns as far as safety and security of this person is involved, then you may apply for private session; but, otherwise, just give us the names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Maznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And in Maznik, where was it that you presented this document? Was it at a -- was it at another store, or was it on the road, or was it somewhere else, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: At the headquarters. It was like an old house. I don't know whether somebody used to live before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And, again, this was a KLA headquarters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After showing the KLA soldier this document that you had got in Rznic, were you allowed to travel on from Maznik to Bucan?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I believe that Mr. Kearney misspoke himself with regard to where he got the travel document. I believe he got the travel document in Ratis, not in Rznic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After you presented this travel document to the soldier in Maznik, were you allowed to pass on to Bucan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said earlier, Witness 4, that at some point after you sought permission to travel you were visited in your home by Togeri and three men who you named earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did they tell you during that visit, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They came and told us, after I'd gone several times to take this document -- I had gone to Zefi and the other person several times, but they did not give me the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And when this person you've identified as Togeri and the three men who you named earlier came to your house, what did they tell you during that visit to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They came to the house. They talked to the mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you hear that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did they tell your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They told my mother that there was -- that no document could be issued to go anywhere, and they told her that if she would go anywhere, she would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did they tell her why this was, that she could not go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After that warning to your mother, did anything happen to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: After some time --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't know. Maybe a week later. I was not counting the days at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please tell us what happened during this next incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: That night, it was after 10.00 at night, Toger came together with a couple of other persons, three or four persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you yourself see Togeri that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, please, tell us how Togeri and the men were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Toger had the same clothes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say "same clothes on," are you referring to the black uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On the uniform, was there a KLA insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I didn't notice that night whether he was armed or not, but all other times he was armed. So maybe he did have a gun that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he wearing a mask or no mask on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No mask, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How were the other men that were with him dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I did not see the others. I only saw a couple of them. The others were outside while he and a couple of others were inside -- well, at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the men -- any of the other men besides the person you described as Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, please, after they came.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: That night they were asking questions about my brother, my eldest brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Without mentioning his name, what was the general nature of the conversation, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They discussed about my older brother. At that time, he was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: After this conversation about your brother, was there any more conversation between the men and yourself or your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: They asked my mother where my brother was because they had heard he had been released from prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did your mother respond to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Yes. She said that as far as we knew, he was still in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: These questions that were being asked about your brother, who was asking them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: Toger asked questions that night about my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Based on your own personal observations, Witness number 4, could you tell who was in charge or command of these men who came over that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04
utterances.text: I don't know about that night. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, we'll move into private session rather than ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am trying, as much as I can, to proceed quickly through this material. I'm reducing the number of exhibits that I'm introducing before the Court. And I understand the time concerns by the Panel. There just happens to be a large amount of material to gain from this witness. I would guess -- I would guess between 60 and 90 minutes I will be completed with my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I take 75 minutes, which is between 60 and 90, if I add to the time you've used already until now, that would bring you considerably over three hours where the witness was scheduled for one hour and a half. I'm not criticising you for not efficiently examining this witness. I'm concerned about all the witnesses until now that have taken approximately anything between one and a half and two times the time, if not more, scheduled for those witnesses. That's my main concern. Then I'd like to ask your attention for another matter, which is the following: It seems that one date is agreed between the parties as a clear date; that was the 2nd of March. If I add all the weeks or the four days or the two weeks, et cetera, this is asked to the witness again and again, two weeks hospital, two weeks until the first search visit, and then another two weeks for the -- well, altogether, if I take always the upper assessment, then I'm somewhere very early June where the witness says it's already autumn. There might be a matter in awareness of time and awareness of what a week is, what a month is, what a day is. And since it confuses, I would like to ask special attention for that aspect, to you and later for the Defence as well. Then we will adjourn for the day -- MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: May I rise? Just a very, very brief matter, just to ensure smoothness. As you know, Mr. Re has handled a good number of issues that tend to arise at the beginning of the day, varying topics and issues that arise, procedural matters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- that arise at the beginning of the day and there may be some tomorrow. He has up until now been dealing with them. If there are any to be raised by the Defence tomorrow that they're aware of in advance, it would be useful to the Prosecution to simply have an idea at least of what topic it is in advance so that I can, or Mr. Kearney can, deal with that tomorrow in the light of the fact that Mr. Re has dealt with so many of them. So I just -- if the Defence can assist, it would assist me in -- or Mr. Kearney, in providing a swifter response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that. At the same time, this Chamber is not much inclined to spend always every day the first 45 to 50, 60 minutes on procedural matters. The parties are -- we did it today, and, of course, it was a bit exceptional, but let's try to reduce the time spent on that in court as much as we can. Try to find solutions outside of court. If really -- it's impossible. I tried to speed up procedural matters in the beginning, but I must admit that I was not very successful. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm certainly not inviting any. I'm just saying if there are to be, a heads-up would assist us to deal with it quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn tomorrow, the 20th of March, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.
